![Appointment Door - Photo by Dima Pechurin on Unsplash https://unsplash.com/photos/white-wooden-door-JUbjYFvCv00](https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/appointment-door-300x169.jpg)[Azul](https://www.azul.com/) has announced the appointment of [Kenny Johnston](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kencjohnston/) as Chief Product Officer. The appointment comes following the retirement of [Martin Van Ryswyk](https://www.linkedin.com/in/martinvr/), after five years in the role. Johnston joins from Luciq, where he was Chief Product and Technology Officer. He has over two decades of experience in technology. His recent roles have seen him gain deep experience of building agentic, AI-powered enterprise DevOps and observability tools and platforms.

At Azul, he will be responsible for leading the product strategy and execution of Azul’s AI-first Java Platform. Moreover, the platform supports, secures, and maintains Java ecosystems that organisations have invested in.

It consists of [Azul Prime](https://www.azul.com/products/prime/), [Azul Core](https://www.azul.com/products/core/), [Azul Intelligence Cloud](https://www.azul.com/products/intelligence-cloud/), [Azul Payara Micro](https://www.azul.com/products/payara-micro/) and [Azul Payara Server](https://www.azul.com/products/payara-server/). Azul Payara Micro and Azul Payara Server were added to the Azul platform through Azul’s December 2025 [acquisition of Payara](https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/2025/12/12/azul-acquires-payara-to-strengthen-java-leadership/).

Johnston will advance the roadmap to meet AI demands on Java estates. He will tackle cost, performance, security, modernization, and productivity head-on. AI pressures now drive every initiative in the enterprise Java landscape.

[Scott Sellers](https://www.azul.com/leadership/scott-sellers/), Co-Founder and CEO, said, _“_ _Kenny’s track record of scaling enterprise product organisations to build products that address business-critical use cases makes him exactly the right product leader as AI reshapes the performance, security and cost demands of every enterprise Java estate_ _._

_“Under his leadership, we’re focused on continuing_ _to build out our AI-first Java platform and helping drive Azul into its next phase of growth_ _.”_

## Who is Kenny Johnston

![Kenny Johnston, CPO, Azul (image credit - LinkedIn/Kenny Johnston)](https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Kenny-Johnston-CPO-Azul.jpg)Kenny Johnston, CPO, Azul

Johnston spent four years at Luciq, first as VP of Product and then as Chief Product and Technology Officer. He led global teams across Customer Success, Support, Product, Design and Engineering functions.

He was responsible for delivering agentic observability built for enterprise mobile developers to help their apps meet the increasingly high bar that mobile users expect. Johnston helped the development function transform using Agentic SDLC with AI tools like Claude Code, FigmaMake, CodeRabbit & HumanLayer.

Before Luciq, he was the Senior Director of Product Management at GitLab for nearly four years, leading a globally distributed Product Management function. He also held product leadership positions at both Rackspace and Hewlett-Packard.

At Rackspace, he served as director of product management for Rackspace Private Cloud. More than tripling annual revenue and earning recognition as HPE’s Global Service Provider Partner of the Year.

At HP, he managed strategy development and feature prioritization for HP Helion – OpenStack Distribution.

Johnston said, _“Java is the backbone of the world’s most critical enterprise systems, and AI is amplifying the pressure on all of it._ _The opportunity is to bring an AI-first, DevOps-centric vision to how Java is developed, deployed, secured and monitored in the enterprise_ _._

_“I’ve spent my career helping world-class teams accelerate through transformative moments like this, and I’m excited to build on the strong foundation Azul has already established_ _.”_

## Enterprise Times: What does this mean

Johnston’s arrival gives Azul a product leader with relevant experience at the point where Java, AI and enterprise modernisation are converging. Azul is arguing that Java will remain central to production AI, not just legacy systems. With Johnston’s background in DevOps, observability and agentic AI, this should help connect that message to practical product execution.

The key test will be whether Azul can turn its AI-first Java platform into measurable benefits around performance, security and cloud cost. If Johnston succeeds, Azul could strengthen its position as enterprises reassess Java estates for the AI era.

Looking forward, Azul’s product roadmap will focus on alleviating the pressures AI places on enterprise Java: absorbing AI workload demand and optimising cloud cost (Azul Prime), narrowing the AI-era security and patch-velocity gap (Azul Core), enabling AI-driven modernisation (Azul Intelligence Cloud, Azul Payara), and giving AI-modernised workloads the scalability, security and automation they need (all Azul products).
